features.description: Lock-time plan-doctor cross-checks — D024 fix. Plan 004 pre-lock review caught two inconsistencies that mid-dispatch discovery would have cost ~9M tokens to learn: (a) child_charter.allowed_paths still pointed at archived axiom/packages/** dirs (predated D006 rename to DontPanic/dashboard/); (b) F001 acceptance #4 demanded a smoke test against <firebase-project-id> with seed Firestore state, but parent_acceptance_item explicitly defers F003-F005 'until operator credentials in place' — an internally contradictory plan. Both shapes are deterministic to detect. Add validate_plan_cohesion() to dontpanic_doctor.py: for each feature with steps[], parse each step for file-path-shaped tokens and warn if they're outside the child_charter.allowed_paths globs; for each acceptance string, flag resource names (<firebase-project-id>, axiom-workspace-*, specific project IDs) that also appear in parent_acceptance_item with deferral language ('deferred', 'until ... in place', 'credential-gated'). Lock-time advisory: WARN findings, doesn't block lock. Surfaces deltas before operator hits paid dispatch.
steps: Read dontpanic_doctor.py current structure + the plan_loader's parsed Plan model shape.

Add validate_plan_cohesion(plan_dir) helper that loads plan.md frontmatter + features.json, walks features[].steps[] looking for path-shaped tokens (regex: `[\w./-]+\.\w+` or backtick-quoted paths), cross-references against child_charter.allowed_paths globs via fnmatch.
Add acceptance-vs-deferred check: scan features[].acceptance strings for resource names that also appear in parent_acceptance_item with deferral markers; warn on hit.
Wire into the existing doctor runner (--include-projects path or a new --validate-plans flag).
Fixture tests covering the plan 004 reproducer (axiom/-only allowed_paths + <firebase-project-id>-acceptance-vs-deferred), plus a clean-plan negative case.
Bonus: emit a copy-paste fix suggestion per finding (e.g. 'add dashboard/** to allowed_paths' or 'rescope acceptance #4 to local-fixture per D-entry').

features.description: Verdict-string vs finding-class reconciliation in supervisor — D022 fix. Plan 010 F002 codex auditor returned audit_status='blocked' because its read-only sandbox couldn't run pytest. Its only finding was severity=advisory, category=test_coverage (non-substantive — exactly what F003's v3 taxonomy classifies as advisory-only, non-blocking). But the supervisor terminated 'blocked after 1 round' because the verdict STRING was 'blocked' — the F003 ENVIRONMENTAL_BLOCKER short-circuit fires on a finding-class, not on the verdict string itself. Reconcile: when auditor returns verdict='blocked' AND ALL findings classify as advisory-only via the v3 taxonomy, promote terminal from blocked-after-N to paused_on_environmental (matching F003 ENVIRONMENTAL_BLOCKER semantics). Don't trust the verdict string alone — trust the findings. Operator currently has to use F004 close --operator-resolved --reason environmental_reproduction_failure manually; F002 makes this automatic.
steps: Read supervisor.py's terminal-decision branch + circuit_breakers.py ENVIRONMENTAL_BLOCKER short-circuit.

Add helper: `is_advisory_only_findings_set(findings, taxonomy_classifier)` → True iff findings is NON-EMPTY AND every finding classifies to environmental_reproduction_failure / evidence_shape_disagreement / spec_ambiguity / scope_overreach (i.e. the advisory v3 classes). Empty-findings is NOT vacuously advisory.

Empty-findings edge case: when auditor returns verdict=blocked AND findings list is empty (network failure, format error, auditor refused to produce findings), treat as a separate `blocked_no_findings` terminal that surfaces 'auditor unable to produce findings — operator review required' via INBOX. Do NOT auto-promote to paused_on_environmental because we have no evidence the blocker is environmental.
In supervisor's post-auditor decision: if verdict=blocked and is_advisory_only_findings_set is True, override terminal to paused_on_environmental + emit reconciliation INBOX event.
Preserve original behavior when findings include any substantive class (implementation_defect, regression, etc.) — substantive findings + verdict=blocked = real blocker.

Fixture tests: (a) replay plan 010 F002 codex envelope (advisory test_coverage) → paused_on_environmental; (b) plan 004 F004 codex envelope (high correctness) → needs_changes unchanged; (c) crafted verdict=blocked + empty findings → blocked_no_findings + INBOX event; (d) crafted verdict=blocked + mix of advisory + substantive → blocked (substantive wins).
features.acceptance: (1) Supervisor reconciles verdict=blocked against finding classification before terminating. (2) Plan 010 F002 codex envelope (advisory test_coverage finding) terminates as paused_on_environmental, not blocked. (3) Plan 004 F004 codex envelope (high correctness finding) still terminates as needs_changes (unchanged behavior on substantive findings). (4) Empty findings + verdict=blocked terminates as `blocked_no_findings`, NOT auto-promoted to environmental (no evidence the blocker IS environmental). (5) Reconciliation INBOX event documents the override + classification.

features.description: Shlex-safe command-string handling — D025 root cause #1. Plan 004 F002 dispatch errored mid-run with 'No closing quotation' (shlex.split parse failure) after the implementer envelope was written but before the codex auditor was invoked. The implementer's prose is untrusted input — its `target_context.commands_run` strings get shlex-parsed somewhere in command_guard's post-hoc validation, and an unbalanced quote in the LLM's output raises ValueError that nothing catches. Audit every shlex.split() call in command_guard.py + prompts.py + supervisor.py + any post-hoc parsing of implementer output. Wrap each with try/except ValueError; on parse failure, emit a structured warning (not crash) into the audit envelope's findings list + skip the affected command. The supervisor must NEVER crash on bad LLM output — it must always reach a terminal.
steps: Grep `shlex.split` across scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/ + command_guard.py + prompts.py. List every call site + caller chain.
For each call site whose input traces back to agent output (implementer summary, auditor findings, target_context.commands_run), wrap in try/except ValueError.

On parse failure: log structured warning, append a 'finding' to the agent's envelope with severity=advisory category=parsing 'shlex parse failed: <message>' + the raw command string (truncated), skip the offending command (don't include it in commands_run validation).
Fixture tests with crafted bad-input strings: (a) unbalanced single quote, (b) unbalanced double quote, (c) unescaped backslash at EOL. Each should produce a warning, not raise.

BACKSTOP — supervisor-level catch: D025 reproducer did NOT pinpoint the offending shlex.split call site. If the exhaustive in-repo audit doesn't surface a call site that reproduces 'No closing quotation' on the plan 004 F002 implementer text, add a top-level `try/except ValueError` around dispatch_volley's iter loop that writes the F004 checkpoint (preserves transactional state) and exits cleanly. This catches shlex failures from dependencies / subprocess output parsers / Pydantic validators that call shlex under the hood — anywhere we don't control.

Replay test: re-run plan 004 F002's exact implementer commands_run through the post-iter pipeline. Volley reaches a real terminal (signed_off / needs_changes / blocked / blocked_no_findings) instead of crashing mid-run.
features.acceptance: (1) Every shlex.split() in the agent-output-parsing pipeline is wrapped with try/except. (2) Bad-input shlex strings produce structured warnings, not unhandled exceptions. (3) Fixture tests cover all three classic shlex failure modes (unbalanced quotes, escape errors). (4) Backstop ValueError catch in dispatch_volley's iter loop handles parse failures from outside our shlex callers (dependencies, subprocess parsers). (5) Plan 004 F002 reproducer test asserts the volley reaches a clean terminal even with the parse-breaking input.

features.description: Supervisor iter-checkpoint artifacts — D025 root cause #2. Even with F003's shlex hardening, the supervisor's post-iter processing has many failure modes (env errors, missing schemas, OSError, etc.) that could leave dispatch in an orphaned state — implementer envelope on disk, no terminal record, operator left to reconstruct from logs (which may be empty due to tee buffering). Wrap each iter (implementer invocation + auditor invocation) in a try/except that, on any failure, writes a `terminal-state-iter{N}.json` artifact recording: exception class + message, what stage failed (implementer / auditor / post-iter validation), what evidence persisted (last-good envelope paths), recommended recovery command (e.g. `dontpanic close --operator-resolved`). Pairs with F003: when shlex catches bad input, the iter still produces a clean failure record.
steps: Read supervisor.dispatch_volley() iter loop + identify exception boundaries.
Add helper `write_iter_checkpoint(plan_dir, iter_n, stage, exception, last_good_paths)` that JSON-serializes the failure context.
Wrap each iter's implementer block + auditor block with try/except Exception; on raise, write the checkpoint + re-raise OR transition to terminal-failed depending on whether the volley can recover.

Decision: re-raise (preserves stack trace for debugging) vs swallow + terminal-failed (cleaner for operator). Default: swallow + terminal-failed, write checkpoint, write transcript entry, exit gracefully.
Fixture test: force a synthetic crash inside the auditor wrapper and assert the terminal-state-iterN.json file is written + the dispatch returns cleanly.
Plan 004 F002 retrospective: replay the dispatch under the new error path and verify the checkpoint includes pointers to the orphaned implementer envelope + the shlex parse error context.
features.acceptance: (1) Every iter wrapped with try/except + checkpoint write. (2) Synthetic-crash fixture produces a terminal-state-iter{N}.json with the expected shape. (3) Dispatch always returns a clean exit code (no unhandled exceptions). (4) Operator-recovery instructions embedded in the checkpoint payload.
